method: Define matching-round token swapping on finite trees; derive edge and vertex capacity inequalities from unique tree paths; construct an m-parameter star family; prove its exact schedule length; independently check path, subdivided-star, double-star, binary-tree and hub-return instances; audit primary-source boundaries.
uncertainty: No constant-factor polynomial schedule relative to LB_0 or LB_hub was proved or refuted.
No unbounded separation between OPT and the strengthened lower bounds was established.
The literature audit supports a bounded source boundary, not a global absence or novelty theorem through all venues.
next_falsifiable_action: Define a dependency-aware lower bound and prove a token-preserving exchange lemma, or construct a hand-checkable tree family separating that lower bound from OPT; do not execute without separate authorization.
mathematical_claim: The universal OPT <= C_max + D + O(1) conjecture is false on arbitrary trees; LB_int is a valid lower bound, and a fixed-hub q+1 return lemma is valid under explicit assumptions.
assumptions: The graph is a finite tree and every vertex is occupied by one distinct token.
A round is a matching of tree edges and swaps occur simultaneously across the matching.
C(e) counts unique source-to-destination paths that contain e.
The fixed-hub strengthening assumes the token initially at v has destination v and q(v)>0.
verified_steps: For the m-leaf star, D=2 and every edge has C(e)=2.
All star edges meet at the center, so at most one can be used per round.
Every star edge must be used and the fixed center token must leave and return, giving OPT>=m+1.
The explicit edge sequence e0,e1,...,e_{m-1},e0 reaches the target, giving OPT=m+1.
Every edge requires at least C(e)/2 swaps and every vertex can participate in at most one swap per round.
gaps: A dependency-aware lower bound capturing jointly dependent detours is not yet defined.
A polynomial-time token-preserving exchange/ordering lemma is not yet proved.

model.move: one matching of E per round; swap tokens across every matching edge
model.objective: minimum number of rounds to realize a target permutation

definitions.path: P_t is the unique source-to-destination path of token t
definitions.edge_crossing_count: C(e)=number of token paths containing e

falsified_claims.claim: OPT <= C_max + D + O(1) on every tree
falsified_claims.witness_family: m-leaf star, m>=2, center token fixed, leaf tokens in one m-cycle
falsified_claims.proof_boundary: For any fixed additive constant K, m+1>2+2+K for m>K+3. Exact schedule: e0,e1,...,e_{m-1},e0.

falsified_claims.witness: two-vertex tree with the two tokens exchanged

proved_claims.proof: Each edge e requires at least C(e)/2 swaps; each vertex can be incident to at most one swap per round; each token moves at most one edge per round.

proved_claims.claim: A fixed hub with q active incident edges requires at least q+1 rounds
assumptions: the token initially at v has destination v
q is the number of incident edges e with C(e)>0

family_audits.result: Adjacent exchange has LB_int=OPT=1; no general path theorem asserted.
Exact OPT=m+1 for the fixed-center leaf cycle.
Same fixed-center return obstruction gives OPT>=m+1, D=4, C_max=2.
Two local fixed-center cycles run independently; OPT=max(p+1,q+1) for the stated instance.
Two disjoint sibling exchanges each require 3 rounds and run in parallel; LB_hub=3.
Local loads compose by maximum when disjoint; bridge traffic leaves unresolved phase-ordering dependence.

upper_bound_assessment.failed_proof_route: Coloring static edge-demand slots does not preserve token identities or occupied-vertex exchange dependencies; the star requires a hub-token return not visible in C and D.
upper_bound_assessment.narrow_surviving_conjecture: A constant-factor algorithm may exist relative to a dependency-aware lower bound extending LB_hub, but the dependency certificate and token-preserving exchange lemma are open.

literature_audit.source: Aichholzer et al., Hardness of Token Swapping on Trees, ESA 2022
literature_audit.finding: Defines parallel rounds as matching swaps, proves NP-hardness on trees including subdivided stars, and describes the arbitrary-tree approximation question as unresolved in that work.

literature_audit.source: Bansal, Günlük, Shapley, Parallel Token Swapping for Qubit Routing, arXiv v2 2025
literature_audit.finding: Gives constant-factor algorithms for cycles, subdivided stars, and grids; Theorem 3 is for subdivided stars. It does not supply an arbitrary-tree approximation theorem.

literature_audit.source: Alon, Chung, Graham, Routing Permutations on Graphs via Matchings, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 1994
literature_audit.finding: The matching-exchange routing model is the same combinatorial move model, but worst-case routing-number bounds do not imply an instance-sensitive C+D theorem.
